item.title: CISA fast tracks SonicWall SonicOS SAML authentication bypass CVE-2026-98001 to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog directives under Binding Operational Directive 22-01, issuing an emergency remediation mandate for an actively weaponized perimeter firewall flaw. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit single sign-on assertion parsing logic to gain administrative access across SSL VPN edge gateways.
The emergency security directive covers SonicWall SonicOS software vulnerability CVE-2026-98001 carrying a CVSS score of 9.8 and impacting Gen 6, Gen 7, and NSv virtual firewalls. Remote unauthenticated threat actors send malformed SAML authentication tokens containing forged identity assertions to bypass multi-factor authentication controls. Successful exploitation grants unauthenticated remote adversaries administrative access to firewall management portals and NetExtender SSL VPN gateways without valid user credentials. Threat telemetry confirms automated scanning arrays actively weaponizing exposed management ports globally. CISA set a mandatory December 17 compliance deadline for Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to deploy updated firmware releases.
Subverting perimeter firewall controllers and secure remote access gateways destroys network perimeter boundaries and internal subnet isolation. Because SonicOS firewalls manage corporate SSL VPN access and site-to-site IPsec tunnels, an unauthenticated SAML authentication bypass permits threat actors to hijack user sessions, inspect encrypted traffic streams, and move laterally across production subnets.
- Upgrade SonicOS firmware installations immediately across physical firewalls and NSv virtual appliances to emergency maintenance releases. - Restrict public internet access to administrative web management portals, placing management interfaces on isolated out-of-band VLANs. - Audit SAML identity provider configuration logs for anomalous authentication assertions originating from unverified IP address ranges. - Invalidate active NetExtender and SMA remote access user session tokens and execute mandatory credential rotations across corporate VPN user accounts.
Perimeter gateway security demands rapid software update deployment and strict out-of-band management isolation to ensure corporate firewall infrastructure remains protected against unauthenticated authentication bypass exploits. #CodeDefence #SonicWall #SonicOS #SAML #AuthBypass #SSLVPN #PerimeterSecurity #CISA #KEV #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Active zero day exploitation targets Ivanti EPMM and MobileIron Core API command injection flaw CVE-2026-127988
item.description:
Enterprise mobile security advisories published today warn of active wild attacks targeting mobile device management infrastructure. Unauthenticated remote threat actors exploit input validation errors within REST API routing subroutines to obtain root remote execution on enterprise MDM servers.
The security bulletin covers Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile EPMM vulnerability CVE-2026-127988 carrying a CVSS score of 9.8. Remote unauthenticated threat actors send crafted HTTP requests containing shell command injection vectors to unauthenticated API endpoints managing device enrollment. Exploitation permits adversaries to execute OS commands under root privileges, deploy persistent web shell backdoors, and exfiltrate corporate mobile enrolment identity certificates. Threat telemetry confirms nation-state threat groups actively targeting exposed EPMM portals worldwide. Ivanti released emergency RPM hotfix packages to mitigate active intrusions.
Subverting central mobile device management controllers undermines fleet-wide mobile security policy enforcement and enterprise access governance. Because Ivanti EPMM manages enterprise mobile enrollment, container encryption keys, and internal app distribution, an unauthenticated root compromise allows threat actors to push malicious mobile payloads, steal corporate credentials, and pivot into corporate subnets.
- Apply official Ivanti RPM security hotfixes immediately across all deployed EPMM server nodes. - Restrict public internet exposure of EPMM administrative and web enrollment portals, enforcing out-of-band access proxies. - Inspect EPMM server file systems and API logs for unverified web shell deployment or anomalous shell command execution. - Invalidate active administrative user session tokens and execute mandatory credential rotations across mobile management accounts.
Mobile management platform defense requires emergency patch application and rigorous file integrity monitoring to ensure enterprise mobile infrastructure remains protected against unauthenticated command execution exploits. #CodeDefence #Ivanti #EPMM #MobileIron #ZeroDay #RCE #CommandInjection #EndpointSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA

item.title: Critical Cisco ASA and Firepower SSL VPN memory leak flaw CVE-2026-76501 exploited in active credential harvesting scans
item.description:
Perimeter network security advisories published today report widespread automated scanning campaigns targeting remote access gateways. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit memory management errors within WebVPN portal parsing subroutines to leak sensitive heap memory contents.
The threat advisory details Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance ASA and Firepower Threat Defense FTD software vulnerability CVE-2026-76501 carrying a CVSS score of 9.1. Unauthenticated remote adversaries send crafted HTTP GET requests to WebVPN authentication interfaces to trigger out-of-bounds heap memory reads. Threat research confirms automated threat arrays are harvesting unencrypted administrative session cookies, user credentials, and active SSL VPN state data from heap memory dumps. Cisco released maintenance updates for ASA and FTD software streams to eliminate the memory leak error.
Subverting perimeter firewall memory structures undermines session confidentiality and secure remote access boundaries. Because Cisco ASA and FTD devices process external SSL VPN user authentications and manage IPsec tunnels, an unauthenticated heap memory leak allows threat actors to harvest valid user session tokens and bypass multi-factor authentication without triggering login alert thresholds.
- Upgrade Cisco ASA and FTD software installations immediately to fixed maintenance releases. - Disable WebVPN and AnyConnect SSL VPN features temporarily if immediate patching cannot be completed across legacy devices. - Monitor WebVPN portal traffic for high-frequency HTTP requests targeting specific internal memory paths. - Force mandatory session logouts and credential resets across all active AnyConnect SSL VPN user accounts.
Perimeter security infrastructure defense demands immediate software update deployment and continuous memory access monitoring to ensure edge VPN gateways remain protected against unauthenticated memory disclosure exploits. #CodeDefence #Cisco #ASA #FTD #SSLVPN #MemoryLeak #WebVPN #PerimeterSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA
